beats: Congratulations! Your new website is ready, and it's one hundred percent yours.
In this short video, we'll put it online, step by step. It takes about ten minutes, it's free, and you don't need any technical skills.
Here's the plan. Unzip your website. Put it on Netlify. Get your own web address. And connect the two.

title: Your two files
caption: Use the “website” file · Keep the “code” file as a backup
beats: First, in your email you received two files.
The one ending in website, is your website. That's the one we'll use today.
The one ending in code, is your backup. Save it somewhere safe, like Google Drive. If you ever hire someone to change your site, give them that file.

title: Unzip your website
caption: Windows: right-click → Extract All   ·   Mac: double-click
beats: Your website comes zipped up in one file, like a parcel. Let's open it.
On Windows, right-click the website file, click Extract All, then click Extract.
On a Mac, just double-click it.
You'll now see a normal folder with the same name. That folder is your website.

title: Create your free Netlify account
caption: netlify.com  →  Sign up  →  use your business email
beats: Next, your website needs a home on the internet. We'll use Netlify, a trusted company that hosts millions of websites. It's free for a site like yours.
Go to netlify dot com, and click Sign up.
Sign up with your business email, then check your inbox and click the link to confirm.
If it asks a few questions about you, answer them, or skip. That's it. The account is yours, in your name.

title: Put your website online
caption: app.netlify.com/drop  →  drag in your FOLDER
beats: Now the fun part. While you're logged in, go to app dot netlify dot com, slash drop.
You'll see a box asking you to drag and drop your folder. Grab the folder you unzipped earlier. The folder, not the zip file. And drop it in.
Wait a few seconds.
And that's it. Your website is live on the internet!
Netlify gives it a temporary address, ending in netlify dot app. Click it to have a look.

title: Get your own web address
caption: Buy it in YOUR name  ·  Turn ON auto-renew
beats: Right now your site has a temporary address. Let's give it your own, like your business dot com dot au. This is called a domain.
It costs around fifteen to twenty five dollars a year. And because you buy it in your own name, it's yours.
We'll use Namecheap, but GoDaddy or Cloudflare work the same way. Search for the name you want. If it's available, add it to your cart, and check out.
Important. Make sure auto-renew is turned on. If a domain isn't renewed, your address stops working.
Australian dot com dot au names need an A B N, so have it ready. Already own a domain? Just log in to where you bought it.

title: Connect your domain
caption: Copy 4 nameservers from Netlify  →  paste into “Custom DNS”
beats: Now let's point your new address at your website. Back in Netlify, open your site, and click Domain management.
Click Add a domain. Type your domain exactly as you bought it, then click Verify, and Add domain.
Netlify will offer to manage your domain. Choose Netlify D N S, and click Continue until you see four nameservers. Keep this page open.
Now open Namecheap. Go to Domain List, and click Manage next to your domain.
Find Nameservers, and change it to Custom D N S.
Paste in the four nameservers from Netlify, one per line. Copy and paste them, so there are no typos. Then click the green tick to save.
On GoDaddy or Cloudflare, look for the same word. Nameservers.

title: You're live
caption: Can take up to 24 hours  ·  The padlock appears by itself
beats: That's everything. Now the internet needs a little time to catch up. Usually a few minutes to a few hours, sometimes up to a day. That's completely normal.
Netlify adds the security padlock all by itself, once your domain is connected.
When you type in your address and your website appears, you're live!
Your website, your hosting, and your domain are all in your name. Congratulations, and thank you for your business!
